title: Mini-map sparkline and hotspots prototype notes
content:
Purpose:
This note captures a focused prototype and interaction spec for adding a horizontally compact mini-map (sparkline) with hotspot markers to the Request Trace view. Goal is to give engineers a fast, scannable overview of where latency and error density are concentrated in a trace and provide keyboard-friendly jump targets that map to span rows in the main waterfall. This doc is intentionally lightweight — sketches, interaction rules, grooming tickets, and acceptance criteria.

Why: problem statement
- Large traces are hard to parse: scrolling to find long tails or clusters of retries is time-consuming.
- Current waterfall only supports coarse zoom and manual pan; users repeatedly open multiple trace tabs to compare segments.
- Support engineers want 1–2 second context switches to get to problem hotspots and attach logs/snapshots.

Prototype components (high level)
1) Mini-map sparkline (top of trace viewer)
   - Single-row compressed timeline showing request token/latency density as a sparkline histogram.
   - X-axis is trace time (start -> end). Y-axis is density (log scale optional) to emphasize spikes.
   - Rendered with thin canvas for performance.
2) Hotspot markers
   - Small clickable markers on the sparkline representing candidate hotspots.
   - Hotspot types: latency spike, error spike, retry cluster, long KV cache miss. Each type uses a subtle color and shape (circle/triangle/diamond).
   - Hover reveals tooltip with: hotspot type, time range, p95/p99 values in that window, example span name.
3) Range selection window (viewport box)
   - Draggable translucent box that shows the current viewport (what is visible in the main waterfall). Dragging adjusts main view and vice-versa.
   - Users can resize to zoom in/out. Double-click center-to-zoom.
4) Hotspot quick-jump and pin
   - Clicking a marker scrolls the main waterfall to the relevant time range and expands the span lane for the top offending span.
   - Users can pin hotspots to create a named snapshot ("Pin and annotate") saved to the trace as a comment link.
5) Keyboard navigation
   - J/K: move to previous/next hotspot.
   - Shift+J/K: move by hotspot type (errors only).
   - Enter: open selected hotspot details panel.
6) Hotspot details panel (side sheet)
   - Small side sheet with a 10–20 span list for the hotspot window, plus actionable links: copy span IDs, open logs, create issue, rerun-simulate.

Interaction rules and microbehaviors
- Sparkline always respects pinned time-range filters (e.g., service-level filter).
- Hotspot detection algorithm runs server-side on trace ingestion, returns candidate ranges with severity score. Client caches per-trace for UI performance.
- Hotspots are clustered visually if within 50ms of each other; cluster marker shows count and aggregate severity.
- Hovering a hotspot shows a faint shimmer in waterfall for corresponding spans (1s fade).
- When viewport box is dragged fast (kinetic), only update main waterfall on release to avoid jank.
- If user clicks a hotspot while a search filter is active, show a small banner: "Jumping to hotspot will clear search filter" with opt to keep filter.

Wireframe notes (visual)
- Layout: top bar (trace metadata) -> mini-map sparkline (24px height) -> main waterfall.
- Colors: use console palette, muted grays for background, amber for latency, red for errors, indigo for retries. Maintain color blind-safe set.
- Markers: 8px diameter for single hotspots, 12px for clusters. Use 1px stroke to separate from sparkline.

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
- Mini-map renders within 50ms for traces up to 5k spans.
- Hotspots are returned for >95% of traces with at least one severity > threshold (configurable).
- Clicking a hotspot navigates the main waterfall and expands the dominant lane to reveal the top span.
- J/K keyboard nav cycles through hotspots in time order and preserves keyboard focus region.
- Pinning a hotspot saves a lightweight annotation object (user, timestamp, note) and shows marker on sparkline.

Open questions / design tradeoffs
- Should hotspots be computed client-side for ad-hoc filters? Client compute gives flexibility but is heavy for large traces. Proposed combo: server precompute base hotspots; client recompute local hotspots for filtered subset only when trace < 1k spans.
- How do hotspots interact with span grouping (by service vs. by resource)? We'll default to timeline-hotspots (global time axis) and include metadata to filter by lane.
- Snapshot storage: attach pins to trace object or as separate lightweight artifacts? Prefer separate "trace-annotations" index for faster retrieval across traces.

Backlog grooming checklist (proposed tickets)
- CONSOLE-NEW-1: mini-map baseline render + viewport binding (3 dev days)
  - UX: static sparkline render.
  - Backend: small endpoint returning per-time-slice density.
- CONSOLE-NEW-2: hotspot detection API + basic markers (4 dev days)
  - Server computes candidate hotspots and returns severity.
- CONSOLE-NEW-3: click-to-jump + expand dominant span (2 dev days)
- CONSOLE-NEW-4: keyboard nav and a11y (3 dev days)
- CONSOLE-NEW-5: pin/annotation persistence + UI (3 dev days)
- CONSOLE-NEW-6: side-sheet hotspot details + log links (4 dev days)
- CONSOLE-NEW-7: client-side recompute for filtered traces <1k spans (2 dev days)

Rough priority / story points
- MVP (1,2,3,4,5) = P0 for Q2 pilot; estimate 17 points.
- Enhancements (6,7) = P1 for Q3; estimate 6 points.

Accessibility notes
- All interactive hotspot markers must be focusable and have accessible names: e.g., "Latency spike 240ms at 00:01.2–00:01.8".
- Keyboard nav must function without mouse.
- Sparkline must have a text summary for screen readers when opened via a context menu (e.g., "Trace contains 3 latency spikes, largest 1.2s at 00:02.1").

Telemetry and metrics to track (post-launch)
- Click-through rate from hotspot -> main waterfall scroll.
- Avg time-to-first-hotspot-click per trace opened.
- Conversion rate: pin created per trace viewed.
- CPU and render time for mini-map across traces.

Prototype testing plan
- Run 6 sessions with SRE and on-call engineers using three real incidents. Observe time-to-first-insight and record suggestions.
- A/B test: mini-map enabled vs. disabled for a beta cohort; measure velocity to problem span.

Notes from 2025-02-20 sketch session (quick highlights)
- Marco: prefer cluster marker with drop-down list of contained hotspots on click to avoid tiny click targets.
- Lena: want a "focus on errors" quick-filter button that jumps to error-only hotspots.
- Rajat: flagged performance concerns for traces >10k spans; recommended soft-fall back to sparse sampling.

Next steps
- Create initial spike PR: simple canvas sparkline + viewport mapping (assign to eng-console).
- UX: produce 2 low-fidelity frames in Figma showing default, clustered, and pinned states.
- Schedule 30m review with SRE/solutions-engineering to validate hotspots shape and usefulness.

References
- link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CONSOLE/Trace+UX+Research+Feb+2025
- figma: https://figma.com/file/trace-mini-map-prototype

(End of notes)
